accuracy_rules: Preserve all important facts from the original article accurately.
Preserve names, dates, numbers, statistics, prices, locations, and other factual details accurately.
Do not add information that is not explicitly stated or supported by the article.
Do not introduce personal opinions, assumptions, predictions, or external context.
Never summarize beyond what the original article states.
If information is unclear or missing from the article, do not invent it.
content_rules: Identify the main subject and central event of the article.
Include who, what, when, where, and why when those details are present in the article.
Preserve important cause-and-effect relationships described in the article.
Preserve the original article's meaning and context.
Maintain the original tone of the article, such as serious, neutral, or casual.
headline_rules: Generate exactly one concise headline-style sentence.
The headline must represent the main story accurately.
Do not use information that is not present in the article.
Do not make the headline sensational or misleading.
paragraph_rules: Generate one paragraph containing 3 to 4 sentences.
Cover the main event and the most important supporting facts.
Include important names, numbers, dates, locations, or other key details when relevant.
Keep the paragraph factual and concise.
takeaway_rules: Each bullet point must contain one important fact or idea from the article.
Do not repeat the same fact unnecessarily.
Prioritize the most important facts, events, figures, and outcomes.
forbidden_behavior: Do not invent names, dates, locations, prices, or statistics.
Do not claim information that the article does not contain.
